own_solution.law: Electronic Zeeman shifts are δE=μ_B B(g_P m_P−g_S m_S), with electric-dipole selection rules Δm=0,±1. The outermost transitions have shifts ±μ_B B(g_P+g_S)/2, giving Δλ=(λ₀²/hc)μ_B B(g_P+g_S). Using μ_B=5.78878×10⁻⁵ eV/T gives Δλ=0.0270061 nm.
assumptions: Use the explicitly specified P3/2 to S1/2 transition.
Use the stated electronic, linear Zeeman model and first-order wavelength conversion.
An added field at the vapour increases the stated field magnitude.

T63F3.regime: The linear weak-field regime requires magnetic shifts much smaller than the fine-structure splitting; the largest P-level shift is approximately 5.79×10⁻⁵ eV, well below 0.0036 eV.

T4FF2.regime: The linear weak-field regime requires magnetic shifts much smaller than the fine-structure splitting; the largest P-level shift is approximately 5.79×10⁻⁵ eV, well below 0.0036 eV.

defect_reasons.other: The alkali principal-doublet P3/2 to S1/2 transition is the shorter-wavelength member, contradicting the problem's identification of it as the longer-wavelength member.
defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T664D and T3EF7 replace the explicit 55 mT quantity in their respective variants TF402 and TD469 with an unspecified 'little', so the variants do not preserve the number and unit.

counterexamples: In the alkali principal doublet, the upper P3/2 level lies above P1/2, so its transition to the common S1/2 lower level has greater photon energy and shorter wavelength.
notes: The numerical solution follows the explicit angular momenta and g-factors despite the incorrect longer-wavelength designation. The compass statements are interpreted as changes confined to the compass field; the earlier-measurement statements do not change the present field. The two fine-structure sentences preserve 0.0036 eV, and the explicitly quantified coil sentences preserve 55 mT; the two 'little' variants do not.
